design_reference: No dedicated wireframe screen — cloud-sync is infrastructure with a small status surface. Anatomy: a low-fi status pill (the design system Badge, good/bad/accent/muted tones) in a corner, reflecting the local-first store's sync state. Light theme, tokens only.

plan.goal: Make the whole app local-first and sync-aware: every write persists locally first, optionally pushes to a cloud transport in the background, and a status surface reflects the sync state — so the editor always works offline and is ready for a real backend without touching feature code.
acceptance_criteria: A CloudSyncService decorates the PersistenceService (Liskov: it IS a PersistenceService) so BookService and every feature are unchanged; it is wired once in createBrain wrapping the local store.
Writes are local-first: get/set/keys/remove hit the local store synchronously, so reads right after a write succeed and the app works fully offline.
When a cloud transport is configured, a write pushes in the background and the sync state moves idle → syncing → synced, or → error if the push fails; the local write is never lost on error.
With no transport configured the store is « offline » (local-only) and emits no per-write noise (status only changes broadcast).

Sync state changes are broadcast on the brain sync:status event; a SyncIndicator surfaces the live state, derived from a status→label/tone Record (KR-117), reading via a useSyncStatus external store (no private copy).

The SyncIndicator renders from design-system tokens/Badge (good=synced, bad=error, accent=syncing, muted=local/idle), is an aria-live status region, and is mounted once by the composition root over both routes.
View-mode/UI state is NOT synced; only the book document flows through the persistence layer (cloud-first boundary, KR-022).
plan.walking_skeleton: createCloudSyncService(local, events, transport?) decorates the local PersistenceService: local-first set (sync write) + a background transport.push that moves the status idle→syncing→synced/error and emits sync:status; with no transport it stays offline (local-only). createBrain wraps the local store with it and exposes brain.sync. useSyncStatus subscribes to sync:status; the cloud-sync feature's SyncIndicator renders the live state as a Badge pill, mounted by App over both routes. The real cloud transport (Cloudflare worker client) + offline write queue are later iterations.

iterations.goal: Real cloud transport: a CloudflareSyncService client (worker route + auth) implementing CloudTransport; debounced batched pushes; last-write-wins reconciliation on book:opened.
Offline write queue: persist pending pushes and flush on reconnect (unblocks book-creation iteration 3); surface a « N changements en attente » state.
Conflict handling: detect divergence between local and cloud, surface a resolution affordance rather than silently overwriting.
Real Cloudflare KV transport: worker proxy, CloudSettingsService credentials UI, user-selectable at runtime via CloudSyncSettings modal.

known_risks: KR-022 — pan/zoom and the canvas↔outline view-mode are UI preferences, NOT part of the synced book document; only the book flows through the persistence layer, so cloud-sync never pushes UI state (avoids spurious conflicts).
KR-011/111 — all persistence still goes through PersistenceService; CloudSyncService is a decorator over it, not a second storage surface; no raw localStorage in feature code.
KR-004 — local-first: the synchronous local write resolves before any event/navigation; the background cloud push must never block or reorder the local write.
KR-117 — the SyncStatus → label/tone mapping lives in one Record (SyncIndicator), derived not branched.

KR-114 — when the real transport lands, any cloud credential/token must be registered in persistenceKeys.ts with a SENSITIVE marker (none yet — the Cloudflare client + auth land with the Cloudflare build target).

iterations_log.label: walking-skeleton
architecture_choices: CloudSyncService is a Decorator over PersistenceService (Liskov, KR-011): createBrain wraps the local store with it and feeds it to BookService, so every feature is sync-aware with zero changes. brain.sync exposes status().

Local-first: set writes local synchronously THEN pushes in the background (KR-004); the status moves idle→syncing→synced/error and is broadcast on a new sync:status event. With no transport the store is offline (local-only) and emits nothing on writes — so the existing 99 tests are fully transparent (no async, no status noise).

useSyncStatus is an external-store subscription over sync:status (KR-013); the cloud-sync feature's SyncIndicator is a VIEW that derives label/tone from a SyncStatus Record (KR-117) and is mounted once by App over both routes.
SyncStatus is a brain type; the CloudTransport interface keeps the real backend swappable (the Cloudflare worker client is deferred).
deviations_from_plan: No real cloud transport in the skeleton — default is local-only (offline). The Cloudflare worker client, debounced batched pushes, reconciliation, the offline queue, and conflict handling are iterations 1–3.
This completes the 0.1.x MVP tier: every feature now has a walking skeleton.

test_coverage.unit: CloudSyncService — local-first delegation, offline (no transport) no-noise, idle→syncing→synced broadcast, error on push failure with the local write preserved
test_coverage.integration: SyncIndicator via brain — « Local » with no transport, syncing→synced after a write with a transport

iterations_log.label: iteration-1
architecture_choices: Per the production-target direction: the « cloud » is selected at the composition root. The LOCAL build target wires a new LocalStorageTransport — a CloudTransport backed by a separate `cloudsync:` localStorage namespace (a fake remote) — so the full local-first machinery runs with no server; the Cloudflare build target swaps in a worker-backed transport (client + worker route + SENSITIVE auth, KR-114) via the same interface later (its CI builds around the full Cloudflare slice). createBrain stays transport-optional so tests default to offline (transparent).

CloudTransport gained an optional pull (for reconciliation). CloudSyncService now DEBOUNCES + BATCHES pushes: set() writes local synchronously then coalesces into a pending map flushed after a debounce window (default 300ms, 0 in tests); status moves syncing (synchronously on write) → synced/error once per batch; the flush timer is tracked + cleared on reschedule (timer-safe).

Last-write-wins reconciliation on book:opened (KR-094): pull the cloud copy, compare updatedAt — a newer cloud copy is adopted by writing the UNDERLYING local store (never the decorated set, so it is not re-pushed — no echo loop) then emitting book:updated so the open view re-reads; a newer local copy is pushed up; an empty cloud is seeded. This is the one place the persistence decorator is book-aware (bookKey + book:updated).
useSyncStatus/SyncIndicator unchanged (KR-013/117). No regression: with no transport (every existing test) the decorator is a transparent synchronous pass-through.
deviations_from_plan: Per user direction, the real Cloudflare client + worker route + auth are deferred to the Cloudflare build target / CI; iteration 1 delivers the transport machinery (debounce/batch + LWW reconciliation) and the local localStorage-backed transport. The Worker Route Parity checklist + KR-114 SENSITIVE token apply when that transport lands (no worker code / credential in the repo yet, so nothing un-deployable is committed).
Reconciliation is last-write-wins by updatedAt (iteration 1); divergence detection + a resolution affordance are iteration 3 (conflict handling). The offline write queue is iteration 2.

test_coverage.unit: CloudSyncService — debounced+batched push (last value per key wins, one syncing/synced), error preserves local, book:opened reconciliation both directions (adopt newer cloud + notify, push newer local up); LocalStorageTransport — push/pull round-trip + separate namespace
test_coverage.integration: SyncIndicator via brain — « Local » offline, syncing→synced after a debounced write

iterations_log.label: iteration-2
architecture_choices: The pending pushes became an OFFLINE QUEUE persisted locally under a new CLOUDSYNC_QUEUE_KEY (in the genliv namespace via the UNDERLYING local store — never the decorated set, no echo; not a book key, so listBooks ignores it). The in-memory pending map is now this persisted Map; it is LOADED at startup, so a write that failed to push survives a reload. A failed push KEEPS the queue (status → error) instead of dropping the batch (the iter-1 behaviour lost it); only the entries actually pushed are dequeued on success (a newer write to the same key during the in-flight push stays queued), guarded by a `flushing` flag against double-push.

Flush-on-reconnect has three triggers: the next write (queuePush reschedules a flush over the whole queue), an explicit retry() (e.g. a reconnect signal), and STARTUP (a persisted backlog schedules a flush). pendingCount() exposes the queue size; a new useSyncPending external-store hook reads it (KR-013), and the sync:status payload gained a `pending` field.

The SyncIndicator surfaces « N changements en attente » (plural() helper) when pending > 0, keeping the status tone (bad on error, accent while syncing) — derived, no new SyncStatus enum value. Emits stay STATUS-change-only (no per-keystroke noise): offline the status toggles syncing↔error per write so the count stays live; an online burst keeps one « syncing » and the count settles on the synced emit.
deviations_from_plan: This UNBLOCKS book-creation iteration 3 (cloud-first offline queue) — the persistence layer now queues + retries; book-creation can build its create-offline flow on top.

`remove` is not queued for cloud propagation (only `set` pushes, as in iter 1) — a synced delete pairs with the conflict/tombstone handling of iteration 3. Divergence detection + resolution affordance remain iteration 3.

test_coverage.unit: CloudSyncService — a failed push queues + persists (pendingCount, local write kept) and a fresh service reloads the backlog; retry() flushes the queue once the transport recovers (pendingCount → 0, synced). Existing debounce/batch/reconcile tests still green.
test_coverage.integration: SyncIndicator via brain — « N changements en attente » when two writes are queued behind a failing transport

iterations_log.label: iteration-3 (conflict handling)
architecture_choices: CONFLICT DETECTION on book:opened reconciliation (KR-098): a conflict is when BOTH sides diverged — local has UNPUSHED edits (the book key is still in the offline queue) AND the cloud copy is NEWER (cloudAt > localAt). In that case reconcile no longer silently last-write-wins: it stashes the cloud copy in a transient in-memory conflictMap (by bookId), does NOT overwrite local, and emits a new sync:conflict event. When local is CLEAN (no queued edit) the existing safe LWW adopt still runs — there are no local edits to lose.

RESOLUTION via CloudSyncService.resolveConflict(bookId, local|cloud): « cloud » writes the cloud copy under the local store (never the decorated set — no echo) + drops the queued local edit + emits book:updated; « local » re-queues the local copy so it pushes over the cloud. Either clears the conflict and re-emits sync:conflict so subscribers re-read. conflicts() lists the books awaiting resolution. resolveConflict is the second book-aware spot in the decorator (like reconcile, KR-094).

The cloud-sync feature gained a ConflictDialog (brain Modal, confirmTone=error) mounted once by App over the editor route: a VIEW over useSyncConflict(openBookId) (external store over sync:conflict, KR-013), offering « Garder ma version » (local) / « Prendre la version du cloud » (cloud). It holds no state and resolves through sync.resolveConflict.
deviations_from_plan: Conflict detection is timestamp+pending based (no per-key version vector): local-pending + cloud-newer is the divergence signal, which is sufficient without a stored base version. Queued DELETES/tombstones (the open question) stay deferred — they need a CloudTransport delete capability that does not exist (same deferral as book-library iter 3 list/delete).

test_coverage.unit: CloudSyncService — detects a conflict (local pending + newer cloud) without overwriting local + emits sync:conflict; clean-local stays safe LWW; resolveConflict cloud adopts / local keeps
test_coverage.integration: ConflictDialog via the feature — surfaces for the open conflicted book, « Garder ma version » keeps local + hides, « Prendre la version du cloud » adopts the cloud book

iterations_log.label: iteration-4 (Cloudflare KV transport + settings UI)
architecture_choices: Real CloudTransport: `createCloudflareKVTransport(workerUrl, syncKey)` — a thin HTTP client that calls a Cloudflare Worker KV proxy. `push` → `PUT /kv/{key}` with JSON body; `pull` → `GET /kv/{key}`, returns null on 404. Auth: `X-Sync-Key` header (the key is base64-encoded inside the worker and used as a KV namespace prefix, so each user's data is isolated without server-side user management).

Worker (`worker/index.ts`) is a minimal KV proxy: GET/PUT/DELETE /kv/{key}, CORS configurable via `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` env var (defaults to * for zero-config). The key is encoded with `btoa` + URL-safe chars to form the namespace prefix `{encodedKey}:{dataKey}`. All 500 errors return a generic message; real message is only in `console.error`.

Credentials are stored in the RAW local store (never the sync decorator) via `CloudSettingsService` (KR-022, KR-114). Two new `persistenceKeys.ts` entries: `CLOUDSYNC_WORKER_URL_KEY` (not sensitive) and `CLOUDSYNC_KEY_KEY` (SENSITIVE — marked with `// SENSITIVE` line comment per KR-114).

`createBrain` gains `cloudSettings: CloudSettingsService` (raw local, never synced). `main.tsx` reads credentials BEFORE calling `createBrain`, picks `createCloudflareKVTransport` when both are present, falls back to no transport (offline) when not configured.

SyncIndicator: `offline` state is now a clickable button that opens `CloudSyncSettings`. `error` state keeps existing retry-button behaviour. `CloudSyncSettings` is a Modal with Worker URL + Sync Key fields, a `Générer une clé` button (crypto.randomUUID), URL validation with `new URL()` try/catch, and a two-step confirmation for the destructive Désactiver action (KR-dangerous-action rule).
`wrangler.toml` + `worker/` give the user everything needed to deploy their own worker to Cloudflare Workers in < 5 minutes.
deviations_from_plan: The plan spoke of a « Cloudflare build target »; instead, the target is user-selectable at RUNTIME via the settings UI — simpler UX (no separate build), no change to Vite config.
No rate-limiting in the worker — the KV namespace is namespaced by the user's own key, so abuse would require knowing the key (accepted risk for a personal tool).

test_coverage.unit: CloudflareKVTransport — push/pull round-trip, 404→null, non-ok throws, trailing-slash strip. CloudSettingsService — get/set/null-clear/isConfigured/round-trip.
test_coverage.integration: CloudSyncSettings modal — URL+key validation, save→reload, Générer key, Désactiver confirmation dialog + clear+reload, Annuler. SyncIndicator — offline button opens settings modal.

open_questions: Queued DELETES / tombstones + cloud-only book list reconciliation need new CloudTransport capabilities (delete + list/enumerate) — deferred (shared with the book-library iter-3 deferral).

Orphaned image KV keys: when a node is deleted locally its image keys become orphaned in KV (the next push removes them from the manifest but does not DELETE the KV entries). Low-impact for now (wasted KV storage); a cleanup sweep needs CloudTransport.delete, deferred.

iterations_log_addendum.label: iteration-5 (KV payload splitting)
architecture_choices: Book payload splitting at the TRANSPORT layer only — local store is unchanged (full book at bookKey). On push, images (node.illustration, pnj.portrait) are extracted into separate KV entries (bookImageKey) and a manifest key (bookImagesManifestKey) tracks which image keys belong to the book. Each key is independently addressable; no full book blob is pushed. The manifest enables an efficient pull: pull content → pull manifest → pull all image keys in parallel → reassemble in memory before writing local.
isRawBookKey() detects the plain book key (no colon suffix after the bookId) so the decorated set() routes books into queueBookSplit() and everything else into queuePush().

Reconcile updated: tries bookContentKey first (validates Array.isArray(nodes) before treating as split format), falls back to legacy bookKey for pre-split books in KV. Legacy books are transparently migrated on the first save after reconcile.
hasPendingBookChanges() and clearBookFromQueue() handle both legacy and split-format queue entries, so conflict detection and resolveConflict() work correctly across both formats.
useBookPending in BrainContext updated to match split keys via startsWith(bookKey(id) + ':') — the check now covers both legacy and split-format pending entries (KR-095).
deviations_from_plan: No new infrastructure or worker routes needed — existing PUT /kv/{key} handles any key shape.

test_coverage.unit: CloudSyncService — 5 new tests in describe('book payload splitting'): routes real Book to split keys; pendingKeys includes split-format entries; extracts illustration+portrait into image keys and strips them from content; reconcile reassembles split-format cloud book with images; resolveConflict('local') with a real Book queues split keys not the legacy key. Plus existing 89 tests green.
